hook.line: Asks what Claude can do that ChatGPT can't, then promises five things.
hook.visual: Face in the top half on a purple-teal backdrop, caption on the seam, a cream card below with the Claude and ChatGPT logos; a gold '5' card at 2.25 s.

beats.what: Question caption on the seam; card below fades in Claude and ChatGPT logo tiles
Card switches to a big gold '5' on black: the list is promised
Checklist card of shared features ('Both now do all of this') before the differences start
Point 1: usage bar with $20 and $200 price pills for Claude's tighter limits
Point 2 title card: gold '2' over 'The vibe'
Screen recording of the record-a-skill dialog with the cursor, proof of the claim
Diagram: one skill branching to Chat, Cowork, Code and Scheduled
Screen recording of Claude Design producing on-brand type samples
Closing card: both logos and 'Which is best? It depends'

why_it_works: The question frames a rivalry most viewers already care about, so the answer feels personally useful
Numbered gold title cards (2, 3) mark progress through the list, so viewers know how much is left
Each spoken claim is backed by a simple card or a screen recording in the lower half, so the face never has to carry the whole 3-minute talk
Fair-minded ending (what ChatGPT does better) builds trust and invites comments
weaknesses: 173 s with one 89 s opening shot and 1.73 cuts per minute; long for TikTok
Follow ask comes at about 4 s, before any value is delivered
90.6% of text sits outside the safe area
for_robert: Borrow the stacked layout: face on top, a cream illustrated card below that changes with each point; Fred could sit on the seam and hold up the gold number card for each list item.
